subject: Cloud Computing
title: GDPR and Cloud Data
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on GDPR and Cloud Data.

hook.text: A European user's data is stored on a U.S. server. Under GDPR, that might be illegal.

buildup.text: GDPR requires companies to protect EU personal data and limits where it can be stored and processed.

discovery.text: Cloud providers offer EU-only regions. Data residency controls ensure data never leaves European borders.

twist.text: GDPR fines are massive: up to 4% of global revenue. Meta was fined $1.3 billion for data transfer violations.

climax.text: Cloud and GDPR coexist, but it requires careful architecture: region selection, encryption, and consent management.

punchline.text: GDPR doesn't ban the cloud. It demands you use it responsibly.

quiz.question: How do cloud providers help customers comply with GDPR?
options: By offering EU-only regions with data residency controls
By automatically deleting all EU user data after 30 days
By making all data publicly accessible for transparency

details.summary: GDPR regulates how organizations collect, store, and process personal data of EU residents, regardless of where the organization is based. In cloud environments, data locality, processing agreements, and cross-border transfer mechanisms require careful configuration.
details.whyItMatters: GDPR violations carry fines up to 4 percent of global annual revenue. Cloud architectures must enforce data residency and processing requirements to avoid severe penalties.
takeaways: GDPR applies to any organization handling EU resident data
Cloud data must be stored in approved regions
Data processing agreements with providers are mandatory

faq.question: Can EU data be stored outside Europe?
faq.answer: Only if adequate safeguards exist, such as Standard Contractual Clauses or the EU-US Data Privacy Framework. Many organizations choose to keep EU data in EU cloud regions to simplify compliance and reduce legal risk from evolving cross-border transfer rules.

faq.question: What is a data processing agreement?
faq.answer: A DPA is a legally binding contract between a data controller and processor that specifies how personal data will be handled. All major cloud providers offer standard DPAs that cover GDPR requirements for data processing, security measures, and breach notification.
